regenerable_on: any host running Traefik 3.x with `--api.insecure=true` and no dynamic providers configured, which is what leaves only the three internal services standing
anonymisation_note: Through the gate, and no substitution was needed: the independent detectors find nothing identifying in any of the five payloads. That is a property of what this variant IS — a Traefik with no dynamic providers publishes only its own internal routers, services and entrypoints, which are identical on every install. The field says the gate ran, not that values were rewritten, and the distinction matters because a reader comparing these payloads against their own Traefik should expect to match them exactly.
note:
The first capture this product has taken from an HTTP interface, and the variant that proved the instance-method seam.

Everything ported before this read a native interface through a module-level function, which is what the replay seam monkeypatches. Traefik reads through an httpx client held on the adapter instance, behind two different fetchers — `_get` for a single document and `_get_list` for the pagination loop that follows X-Next-Page — and stubbing only the first would leave the loop calling the live client against whatever URL the replaying machine happens to have in its environment. Both are stubbed, keyed by request path, which is why the payload files are named for the paths they answer.

The ruleset here is deliberately bare: no dynamic providers, so the only routers and services are Traefik's own internal ones. That is not a thin capture, it is the universal one — api@internal, dashboard@internal and noop@internal are present on every Traefik that has ever run, and they are what found the defect this variant now pins.

Stated bound: with no dynamic provider there is no loadBalancer block on any service, so `Servers`, `ServersUp`, `ServersDown` and `DownServers` are emitted by nothing here, and neither is the URL userinfo redaction that guards them. A capture from a Traefik fronting real backends is the other half of this collector and does not exist yet.
anchors_note:
Read off the payloads by hand, before any stream was generated.

The two absent_fact anchors on noop@internal are the point of this variant and the reason it exists at all. Traefik's internal services carry no `type` member, and `service_facts` published `"Type": null` for three of three services on a stock install — a value the contract's recursive fact_value refuses and the replay judge refuses, because value, absent and unobservable are three statements with three channels and a null names none of them. It survived until now because the queue's provisional ruling on null facts rested on the shape being reachable from no real interface, and it is reachable from the first Traefik anybody points this at. Anchoring the ABSENCE rather than the emission is what makes a regression to null print red, since an anchor asserting a null value would be asserting the unassertable.

noop@internal is anchored for UsedBy too because nothing references it, so the row must carry neither key — while api@internal is used by its own router and carries UsedBy with one entry. The pair is what separates "the collector omits keys correctly" from "the collector omits keys always".

The anchored Priority is two below 2^63, which makes it the number this corpus has that a float round-trip destroys: decoded through a float64 it comes back rounded up to 2^63 exactly, and typed equality catches that where an eyeball would not. It is the reason the pass-through-numbers ruling exists, sitting in a real document from a real service rather than in a hypothetical.
